summary: Pause no longer kills autoplay: the voice-death monitor misread an intentional pause as a dead connection and tore the session down with zero notification.
details: The death monitor (voice_session.py) probes every 5s: a track is loaded AND `is_playing()==False` for two consecutive ticks means 'dead'. `pause()` clears discord.py's `AudioPlayer._resumed`, so `is_playing()` returns False for the whole pause — a paused track tripped the false-positive death path after ~10s. Found live 2026-09-15: pause clicked 13:30:21, monitor declared the connection dead 13:30:30, both reconnect attempts failed with `discord.ClientException: Already connected to a voice channel.` (the connection was ALIVE), and the session was torn down. The room heard nothing.

Fix 1 — `DiscordVoiceSession` tracks `_paused`; the monitor treats an intentional pause as healthy while the websocket is open, and still probes the websocket during a pause so a REAL closed-ws death is never suppressed. `play()` clears the pause flag so a skip after pause re-arms monitoring for the next track.

Fix 2 — `_try_reconnect` recognises `Already connected to a voice channel.` as a false-positive death probe ONLY when the websocket agrees it is open. The exception alone is discord.py's guild→voice-client registry bookkeeping, which survives a truly dead websocket — a closed ws with stale registration still reaches teardown (Codex review MAJOR-1).

Fix 3 — `MusicPlayerManager._leave(..., announce=True)` announces the teardown with `connection_lost_line()` ('Music stopped — voice connection lost. Use /music play to restart.'). Only the voice-death path passes `announce=True`; `/music stop` already replies `Stopped.` and idle timeouts are expected silence, so they do not double-post. Announcement is idempotent — a second `_leave` on an already-torn guild has no player and stays silent.

Tests: the fake voice client now reproduces real discord.py pause semantics (`is_playing()` False while paused, `_resumed` cleared/set; `play()` permitted while paused like the real AudioPlayer), five new session tests (monitor silent while paused and re-armed after resume; reconnect survives an 'Already connected' false-positive with open ws; closed ws + 'Already connected' still tears down — Codex MAJOR-1 regression; pause→skip re-arms monitoring — Codex MAJOR-2 regression) and three new manager tests (voice-death leave announces; plain leave stays silent; no double-post).
limitations: The announce line is only as good as the notify closure — a session whose originating channel is no longer messageable logs a warning and drops it, matching the existing now-playing path.

A REAL voice death while paused with an open-websocket-but-dead-audio-thread is not distinguishable from an intentional pause until someone resumes — the same known R-66 blind spot that predates this change.
